definition: Astroinformatics is an interdisciplinary field of study involving the combination of astronomy, data science, machine learning, informatics, and information/communications technologies.
details: The field is closely related to astrostatistics. Data-driven astronomy (DDA) refers to the use of data science and machine learning techniques to analyze large astronomical datasets produced by telescopes and other observation platforms.

explainer.lead: Astroinformatics helps astronomers learn from the enormous datasets produced by telescopes and other observation platforms. It brings astronomy together with data science, machine learning, informatics, and information and communications technologies.

tiers.eli5: Telescopes can collect more pictures and measurements than people could reasonably study one by one. Astroinformatics is like giving astronomers very clever sorting and pattern-finding helpers, so they can explore all that information and learn about the sky.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners apply data science and machine learning techniques to large datasets from telescopes and other observation platforms. The work sits at the intersection of astronomical questions, data management, analysis, and communications infrastructure; closely related statistical work falls under astrostatistics.
tiers.paperLevel: Astroinformatics = astronomy + data science + machine learning + informatics + information and communications technologies. It is closely related to astrostatistics, while data-driven astronomy (DDA) specifically denotes the use of data science and machine learning to analyze large astronomical datasets.

explainer.example: A telescope produces a very large collection of sky observations. Researchers use data science and machine learning techniques to analyze the collection for patterns, then interpret the results in an astronomical context.

usedIn.name: Astronomy research
usedIn.detail: Combines computational and information methods with astronomical analysis.

usedIn.name: Telescope data analysis
usedIn.detail: Applies data science and machine learning to large observational datasets.

usedIn.name: Data-driven astronomy
usedIn.detail: Uses large datasets from telescopes and other observation platforms as the basis for analysis.

explainer.intuition: Modern astronomy produces data on a scale that calls for more than manual inspection. Astroinformatics supplies the computational methods and information systems needed to turn those observations into analyzable knowledge.
howItWorks: Telescopes and other platforms collect observations.
The observations form large astronomical datasets.
Informatics and communications technologies support the data.
Data science and machine learning analyze the datasets.
Astronomical domain knowledge guides and interprets the analysis.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives astronomy a way to work with datasets whose size makes large-scale computational analysis essential, connecting observation with data-driven discovery.
misconceptions: It is not machine learning alone.
Astrostatistics is closely related, not an unrelated field.
DDA specifically emphasizes data-driven analysis of large astronomical datasets.

diagram.caption: Astroinformatics connects observation, data infrastructure, computational analysis, and astronomical interpretation.
